To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the mental model of a search engine elicited from users is not a realistic model of how the search engine actually works.
the generic mental model of the search interface elicited from users' heuristic evaluations is based on a comparison with a generic mental model of Web search engines.

users' mental model of a digital library search engine is based on the Web search engine ideal model, but that the ideal model is idealistic rather than based on realistic experience with Web search engines.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a method for eliciting mental models of digital libraries.
the development of a methodology for the user-centered elicitation of generic mental models.
the mental models of users of digital libraries and their search engines, and how these mental models are formed and used.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the method presented in this paper can be used to obtain a generic model of users' mental models for a digital library's functionality.
mental model elicitation is not an easy or straightforward process, and it is not always possible to obtain the desired results.
mental models are important for understanding the users' perception of a digital library and for designing interfaces that are easy to use.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mental model of a search engine is a mental representation that users generate in their minds to understand how a search engine works.

the mental model of a search engine can be elicited from a heuristic evaluation of its usability, but the resulting model should not be taken as an ideal model, but as a starting point for further design and development.
the mental models of users are a good source for the design of digital libraries.
The main takeaway from our work is that
users have mental models of the digital library search engine, which can be elicited and analyzed.
mental models can be used to inform the design process, but that the models elicited from users are often idealistic and not realistic.
the design process should not only focus on what is technically possible, but also on what is possible in the user's perception of a digital library.
